answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when its signed actions prove fraudulent. A kernel of independent validators checks evidence before penalties, so an attacker cannot cheaply multiply accounts and vote itself legitimate: every Sybil must lock real capital, and coordinated abuse risks losing it. The garden of agents can still admit newcomers, while an island of isolated test accounts earns no influence until it builds costly, verifiable history.
